decision: Implement POST /api/products/{productId}/images/{imageId}/delete behind the existing employee authorization boundary. The repository deletes the product-scoped database row and returns its filename before the service removes the corresponding media file using a storage Delete operation.
rationale: Product editing routes use POST action-style delete paths and RequireEmployee. ProductImage fields ID, ProductID, Filename, and CreatedAt remain because they are used by persistence, API serialization, media-path construction, and order image snapshots; no field is removed.
consistency: Database deletion precedes filesystem deletion as requested. The service validates the returned product and filename and confines deletion to MEDIA_ROOT/images/products/{productId}; a storage failure is surfaced rather than reported as success, with the unavoidable filesystem/database atomicity limitation documented.
breaking_change: No existing endpoint or response is removed. This adds one employee-only endpoint and one repository/migration function. Existing ProductImage JSON remains unchanged.
unrelated_changes: Announcement changes in the worktree are out of scope and are not modified.
